advances: For the specified original entropy-row family, the original integer means force uniform bounds on both deficit parameters. The entire original law then has uniformly nondegenerate directional covariance and a uniform fourth-moment ratio. Arbitrary independent products retain the same fourth-moment constant and have an absolute halfspace probability cap at their feasible original full mean. This is a theorem for this row family, not a conclusion about all entropy rows or all mixed-integer convex bodies.
author: research-agent
proof:
First establish the original law and its exact parameterization. For integer \(h,L\), nonnegative integers \(x,y\) with \(x+hy\le L\) give the nonnegative integer \(a=L-x-hy\). Conversely, nonnegative integers \(a,y\) with \(a+hy\le L\) give the nonnegative integer \(x=L-a-hy\). These inverse maps prove the stated support bijection. Under the prescribed original means, \(\mathbb EA=L-(L-h-1)-h=1\) and \(\mathbb EY=1\); conversely, these two deficit means imply both prescribed original means.

Let \(\mathcal T=\{(a,y)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{2}:a+hy\le L\}\) and \(Q=\lfloor L/h\rfloor\). The triangle with vertices \((0,0),(L,0),(0,Q)\) lies in \(\operatorname{conv}\mathcal T\). Here \(Q\ge14\), \(L\ge28\), and \(1/L+1/Q\le3/28<1\). Hence \((1,1)\) is in the interior of that triangle, and thus in the interior of \(\operatorname{conv}\mathcal T\). Define
\[
F(t_1,t_2)=\log\!\left(\sum_{(a,y)\in\mathcal T}e^{t_1a+t_2y}\right)-t_1-t_2.
\]
Because \((1,1)\) is interior, some Euclidean ball of radius \(\delta>0\) about it lies in \(\operatorname{conv}\mathcal T\). For \(t=(t_1,t_2)\), the maximum of \(t\cdot(z-(1,1))\) over \(z\in\mathcal T\) is at least \(\delta\lVert t\rVert\). Consequently \(F(t)\ge\delta\lVert t\rVert\), proving coercivity. Its Hessian is the covariance matrix of \((a,y)\) under the positive weights proportional to \(e^{t_1a+t_2y}\). The support contains \((0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\); every nonzero linear functional therefore has positive variance. The Hessian is positive definite everywhere. Thus \(F\) has one and only one minimizer. At it, the two first derivatives vanish, exactly giving full-law means \((1,1)\). Setting \(r=e^{t_1}\) and \(s=e^{t_2}\) gives the positive law and the two stated equations. Strict convexity gives uniqueness of the parameters and of the positive exponential law.

For completeness, write this law as \(p(a,y)=e^{t_1a+t_2y}/Z\). Every other law \(q\) on \(\mathcal T\) with means \((1,1)\) obeys
\[
\sum_{q(a,y)>0}q(a,y)\log\frac{q(a,y)}{p(a,y)}
=H(p)-H(q)\ge0.
\]
Indeed, \(-\log z\ge1-z\) gives a lower bound of \(1-\sum_{q(a,y)>0}p(a,y)\ge0\) for the sum. Equality holds only when the support is all of \(\mathcal T\) and \(q=p\). This proves the entropy characterization. The support bijection preserves entropy. Substituting \(a=L-x-hy\) into the density gives \(\lambda=-\log r\), \(\eta=\log s-h\log r\), and original partition function \(e^{\lambda L}Z\). This substitution changes neither probabilities nor means.

Next bound the parameters using only the two original deficit means. For an integer \(N\ge0\) and \(t>0\), let \(g_N(t)\) denote the mean of the law on \(\{0,\ldots,N\}\) with weights proportional to \(t^k\). It is nondecreasing in \(t\), since its derivative is the variance divided by \(t\). It is increasing in \(N\), since adding the point \(N+1\) adds a value strictly above the old mean. For \(0<t<1\), summing and differentiating the finite geometric series gives
\[
g_N(t)=\frac{t}{1-t}-\frac{(N+1)t^{N+1}}{1-t^{N+1}}.
\]
In particular, \(g_7(2/3)=10562/6305>3/2\), because \(21124>18915\).

The conditional original law of \(A\) given \(Y=y\) has weights \(r^a\) for \(0\le a\le L-hy\). Since \(Y\) is a nonnegative integer and \(\mathbb EY=1\), \(\mathbb P(Y\le2)\ge2/3\). Whenever \(y\le2\), the conditional cutoff is \(L-hy\ge12h\ge24\ge7\). If \(r\ge2/3\), its conditional mean on each such row would be at least \(g_7(2/3)>3/2\). Nonnegativity of the remaining conditional means would then imply \(\mathbb EA\ge(2/3)g_7(2/3)>1\), a contradiction. Therefore \(r<2/3\).

The conditional original law of \(Y\) given \(A=a\) has weights \(s^y\) for \(0\le y\le\lfloor(L-a)/h\rfloor\). Similarly, \(\mathbb P(A\le2)\ge2/3\). For \(a\le2\), its cutoff is at least \(\lfloor14-2/h\rfloor\ge13\ge7\). If \(s\ge2/3\), the same calculation would give \(\mathbb EY>1\), another contradiction. Therefore \(s<2/3\).

Now both parameters lie below one. For every finite cutoff, the displayed formula gives \(g_N(r)<r/(1-r)\). Averaging over all original \(Y\)-values yields \(1=\mathbb EA<r/(1-r)\), whence \(r>1/2\). Averaging the corresponding inequality for the conditional \(Y\)-means gives \(s>1/2\). These arguments use conditional means only to estimate the full-law parameters; no component is assigned the full mean. Finally, \(r^h\le r^2<4/9<1/2<s\), so the original transverse tilt \(\eta=\log(s/r^h)\) is strictly positive.

The partition function and fixed-support probabilities now satisfy \(Z\le\sum_{a,y\ge0}r^as^y=1/((1-r)(1-s))<9\). Both \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\) belong to \(\mathcal T\), and their original probabilities are respectively \(r/Z>1/18\) and \(s/Z>1/18\). Since \(\mathbb ED=0\), retaining just these two contributions to \(\mathbb ED^2\) gives \(\mathbb ED^2\ge(u^2+v^2)/18\).

To bound moments under the complete law, let \(G\) have the untruncated geometric law \(\mathbb P(G=k)=(1/3)(2/3)^k\) for \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). A geometric law of parameter \(t<1\), truncated to \(0,\ldots,N\), has cumulative probability \((1-t^{k+1})/(1-t^{N+1})\ge1-t^{k+1}\) at every \(0\le k\le N\). It is therefore stochastically dominated by the untruncated geometric law of parameter \(t\). For \(t\le2/3\), that untruncated law is itself dominated by \(G\), as seen from its tail probabilities \(t^k\le(2/3)^k\). Applying this to every conditional row and column and averaging their tail probabilities proves that each of the original marginals \(A\) and \(Y\) is dominated by \(G\).

The probability generating function of \(G\) is \(1/(3-2z)\). Differentiation at \(z=1\) gives the falling-factorial moments \(\mathbb E(G)_k=k!2^k\), where \((G)_k=G(G-1)\cdots(G-k+1)\). The polynomial identities \(G^2=(G)_2+G\) and \(G^4=(G)_4+6(G)_3+7(G)_2+G\) give \(\mathbb EG^2=8+2=10\) and \(\mathbb EG^4=384+288+56+2=730\). Thus each of \(\mathbb EA^2,\mathbb EY^2\) is at most \(10\), and each of \(\mathbb EA^4,\mathbb EY^4\) is at most \(730\). The exact original means give \(\mathbb E(A-1)^2,\mathbb E(Y-1)^2\le9\). For a nonnegative integer \(k\), \((k-1)^4\le k^4+1\), so \(\mathbb E(A-1)^4,\mathbb E(Y-1)^4\le731\).

Pointwise Cauchy-Schwarz and \((z_1^2+z_2^2)^2\le2(z_1^4+z_2^4)\) now yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb ED^2&\le(u^2+v^2)\mathbb E\bigl((A-1)^2+(Y-1)^2\bigr)
\le18(u^2+v^2),\\
\mathbb ED^4&\le2(u^2+v^2)^2\mathbb E\bigl((A-1)^4+(Y-1)^4\bigr)
\le2924(u^2+v^2)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Together with the covariance lower bound, the last expression is at most \(2924\cdot18^2(\mathbb ED^2)^2=947376(\mathbb ED^2)^2\). These statements also hold when \(u=v=0\). The original centered identity in the statement follows directly from \(X=L-A-hY\); it maps a nonzero original normal to a nonzero pair \((-b,c-hb)\), proving the claimed full-law directional result in original coordinates.

For the independent product, denote the centered summands defining \(T\) by \(T_j\) and their variances by \(V_j\). Each has mean zero and fourth moment at most \(KV_j^2\), irrespective of its parameters or normal. Independence and centering give
\[
\mathbb ET^2=\sum_jV_j,\qquad
\mathbb ET^4=\sum_j\mathbb ET_j^4+6\sum_{i<j}V_iV_j
\le K\left(\sum_jV_j\right)^2,
\]
where the inequality uses \(K\ge3\). The constant is applied once after summing the independent block variances, so it acquires no dependence on the number of blocks.

If \(\sigma^2=\mathbb ET^2>0\), Holder's inequality applied to \(|T|^{2/3}|T|^{4/3}\) gives \(\sigma^2\le(\mathbb E|T|)^{2/3}(\mathbb ET^4)^{1/3}\), hence \(\mathbb E|T|\ge\sigma/\sqrt K\). For \(T_+=\max(T,0)\) and \(T_-=\max(-T,0)\), centering gives \(\mathbb ET_+=\mathbb ET_-=(1/2)\mathbb E|T|\). Cauchy-Schwarz gives \(\mathbb ET_+\le\sigma\sqrt{\mathbb P(T>0)}\) and \(\mathbb ET_-\le\sigma\sqrt{\mathbb P(T<0)}\). Consequently each strict one-sided probability is at least \(1/(4K)\). If \(\sigma^2=0\), the nonnegative variable \(T^2\) has mean zero, so \(T=0\) almost surely. In fact the positive covariance bound and independence show this case occurs exactly when all original block normals vanish.

Finally, \((L_j-h_j-1,1)\) has nonnegative integer coordinates and satisfies \((L_j-h_j-1)+h_j=L_j-1\le L_j\), so the full mean \(\boldsymbol\mu\) belongs to the original product support. Write a closed halfspace containing it as \(H=\{z:w\cdot(z-\boldsymbol\mu)\ge a\}\), with \(a\le0\). The centered projection \(w\cdot(z-\boldsymbol\mu)\) is a sum \(T\) with arbitrary original block normals. If its variance is positive, \(\{T>0\}\subseteq H\), proving the claimed cap. If its variance is zero, the product lies in \(H\) almost surely. All probabilities here belong to the original product of the original exponential rows, and all means are their exact original full means.
statement:
Let \(h,L\) be integers with \(h\ge2\) and \(L\ge14h\), and set \(E_{(L,h,1)}=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{2}:x+hy\le L\}\). There is exactly one strictly positive exponential probability law on this original set having original mean \(\mathbb E(X,Y)=(L-h-1,1)\). It is also the unique Shannon-entropy maximizing law among all probability laws on this set having that mean.

Define the original deficit \(A=L-X-hY\). The map \((X,Y)\mapsto(A,Y)\) is a bijection from \(E_{(L,h,1)}\) to \(\{(a,y)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{2}:a+hy\le L\}\), and \(\mathbb EA=\mathbb EY=1\). The original probability law is
\[
\mathbb P(X=x,Y=y)=\frac{r^{L-x-hy}s^y}{Z(r,s)},\qquad
Z(r,s)=\sum_{y=0}^{\lfloor L/h\rfloor}s^y\sum_{a=0}^{L-hy}r^a.
\]
The positive parameters \(r,s\) are uniquely specified by the two full-law equations \(r\partial_r\log Z=s\partial_s\log Z=1\), and satisfy \(1/2<r,s<2/3\), in particular the requested bounds \(1/2\le r,s<3/4\). In original exponential coordinates the same law has density proportional to \(e^{\lambda x+\eta y}\), where \(\lambda=-\log r\) and \(\eta=\log s-h\log r>0\).

For every \(u,v\in\mathbb R\), put \(D=u(A-1)+v(Y-1)\). With all expectations taken under the entire original law,
\[
\frac{u^2+v^2}{18}\le\mathbb ED^2\le18(u^2+v^2),\qquad
\mathbb ED^4\le2924(u^2+v^2)^2\le K(\mathbb ED^2)^2,
\quad K=947376.
\]
Thus the full-law covariance of \((A,Y)\) lies between \((1/18)I_2\) and \(18I_2\) in the positive-semidefinite order. For any original normal \((b,c)\),
\[
b\bigl(X-(L-h-1)\bigr)+c(Y-1)
=-b(A-1)+(c-hb)(Y-1),
\]
so the same fourth-moment ratio \(K\) holds for every original directional projection.

For every integer \(m\ge1\), take independent original rows \((X_j,Y_j)\) as above, allowing arbitrary integers \(h_j\ge2\) and \(L_j\ge14h_j\). Their original product mean is the feasible integer point \(\boldsymbol\mu=((L_j-h_j-1,1))_{j=1}^{m}\). For every closed halfspace \(H\subseteq\mathbb R^{2m}\) containing \(\boldsymbol\mu\), the original product law satisfies \(\mathbb P(((X_j,Y_j))_{j=1}^{m}\in H)\ge1/3789504\). The constant is independent of \(m\), all \(h_j,L_j\), and every original block normal. More precisely, for any real coefficients \(b_j,c_j\), the centered sum
\[
T=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\left[b_j\bigl(X_j-(L_j-h_j-1)\bigr)+c_j(Y_j-1)\right]
\]
satisfies \(\mathbb ET^4\le K(\mathbb ET^2)^2\). If \(\mathbb ET^2>0\), each of \(\mathbb P(T>0)\) and \(\mathbb P(T<0)\) is at least \(1/(4K)=1/3789504\). If \(\mathbb ET^2=0\), then \(T=0\) almost surely.
